# Design: Forward-compatible configuration

## Context

- `codev-engine::config::ProjectConfig` and its nested `McpConfig`,
  `ChangelogConfig` and `InheritSource` all carry
  `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`; `config::load` turns any serde error into
  `EngineError::Invalid` (code `invalid`). Every command reads the file
  through `config::load` or `config::resolve`, so one unknown key stops
  them all, `codev doctor` included.
- `config::resolve` already returns non-fatal `warnings` (inherited sources)
  that `codev status`, `codev new change`, `codev init` and `codev update`
  report, in human output and in the JSON `status` array.
- `codev validate` reports items of kind `change`, `spec` and `decisions`;
  `--strict` fails on any warning finding.
- `codev doctor` gathers `DoctorFacts` in the CLI and `codev-core::doctor`
  evaluates them (decision 0001). Its `codev_version` check always gives the
  fix `codev self-update`, while `codev self-update` refuses a downgrade
  without `--version` (`codev-core::update::decide`). The update cache only
  records the latest release, not a list of releases.
- codev 0.5 and earlier ship the strict parser: nothing done here changes
  how they read a newer configuration.

## Goals / Non-Goals

Goals: an older codev (from this release on) keeps working on a newer
configuration and says what it needs; typos at the top level stay visible
and fail `codev validate --strict`; doctor's version fix is a command that
works.

Non-goals: tolerating unknown keys in other files (`change.yaml`,
`schema.yaml`, `seal.yaml`, whose strictness is unchanged); a
`--version` fix for the "below" case; fetching the release list to find
the highest satisfying release (doctor stays offline).

## Decisions

### Decision: Tolerance per section, by what ignoring a key would do

The criterion: a section is tolerant when ignoring an unknown key only
means "this feature is absent", and strict when ignoring it would make
codev silently do something different from what the file asks.

| Section | Unknown key | Why |
|---|---|---|
| top level | warning | each top-level key is an independent feature; ignoring one leaves the others intact, and the top level is where a newer codev adds keys (`codev_version` was one) |
| `mcp` | warning | built to grow (one tool name per integration); ignoring an unknown tool only leaves that integration unconfigured, which the skills already handle with their "not configured" fallback |
| `inherits` entries | error | an entry identifies a source; ignoring a key (a future pin, filter or subpath variant) would read a different source than intended and inject its context into prompts (decision 0005: inherited content is security-sensitive) |
| `changelog` | error | `codev changelog --write` rewrites `CHANGELOG.md`; ignoring a key that narrows or reshapes the output would write a different file without saying so |
| `rules` | not applicable | a free map of artifact ids, already open |

The top level and `mcp` lose `deny_unknown_fields`; `InheritSource` and
`ChangelogConfig` keep it. Unknown keys are found by reading the file a
second time as a generic YAML mapping and comparing its keys with the known
lists (`PROJECT_KEYS`, `MCP_KEYS`), declared next to the structs. A test
loads a configuration holding every known key and asserts that none is
reported, so a field added to a struct without its name fails a test.

Inherited sources are parsed with the same tolerant code, but their unknown
keys are dropped silently: only their `context` and `rules` are read, every
other key — known or not — is already ignored.

**Alternatives considered**: `#[serde(flatten)] extra: BTreeMap<…>` on
`ProjectConfig` — rejected: flatten buffers the whole map and degrades
serde's error messages for every nested field, which decision 0006 values
for hand-written YAML; it also does not reach into `mcp`. The
`serde_ignored` crate — rejected: a new dependency for what a comparison of
two key lists does. Tolerating every section — rejected for `inherits` and
`changelog` for the reasons in the table. Keeping everything strict and only
improving the error message — rejected: the old binary would still be
unusable, which is the problem.

### Decision: One warning per key, built from the file alone

`config::load` returns the unknown keys (dotted for `mcp`: `mcp.design_tool`)
with their line, found by scanning the text for `key:` at the right
indentation (line 1 when not found, e.g. a flow mapping). `config::resolve`
turns each project key into a `Warning { code: "unknown_config_key" }`
whose message names the key, says the project may need a newer codev,
quotes `codev_version` when the file sets it and points to
`codev self-update`, or to correcting a typo. The message does not name the
running version: the engine does not know it, and the doctor check and
`versionRequirement` already compare versions.

When the strict parse fails (a nested strict section, a wrong type), the
error is enriched the same way: the file is read leniently as a YAML
mapping and, if it holds a string `codev_version`, the message adds
"this project requires codev_version: "…"; run `codev self-update` if your
codev is older". The code stays `invalid`.

**Alternatives considered**: one warning listing all keys — rejected: one
finding per key gives each its line in `codev validate`, and JSON consumers
match on one code per fact. A dedicated error code for the enriched error —
rejected: the failure is still an invalid file; the hint is in the message.

### Decision: A `config` item in `codev validate`, present only when needed

`validate_all` appends an `ItemReport` of the new kind `ItemKind::Config`
(`"config"` in human and JSON output), path `_codev/config.yaml`, with one
`Warning` finding per unknown key, only when there is at least one. The
scoped runs (`--changes`, `--specs`, a named item) do not include it: they
are about one kind of item.

A warning, not an error, so plain `codev validate` (the pre-commit and
teammate case) passes while `codev validate --strict` (CI) fails: in CI, an
unknown key is either a typo — which must not slip through now that it no
longer fails parsing — or a CI codev older than the configuration, which
must be updated. The `kind` value is additive to the v1 contract; consumers
that switch on `kind` already face three values.

**Alternatives considered**: always emitting the item, empty when clean —
rejected: it changes every existing report and test for no information.
An error finding — rejected: it would make the older teammate's plain
`codev validate` fail, the situation this change removes.

### Decision: A `config.keys` doctor check, a warning

A new check `config.keys` in the Configuration group, right after
`config.language`: `ok` when the project's configuration has no unknown
key, otherwise a `warning` with the code `unknown_config_key`, a message
naming the keys, and a fix that depends on the version check: `codev
self-update` when the running codev does not satisfy `codev_version`,
otherwise "correct or remove the key in `_codev/config.yaml`, or run
`codev self-update` if a newer codev added it". A warning, because the
command works and doctor's `--strict` fails only on what is missing.

**Alternatives considered**: folding the keys into `config.rules` or
`validate` — rejected: the check would mean two things, and its code would
not say which.

### Decision: The downgrade target is computed in the core

`codev-core::update` gains `requirement_side(requirement, current)`
(`Below` / `Above`, `None` when satisfied or unparsable) and
`downgrade_target(requirement, latest_known)`. A comparator that fails
marks `Above` when it is an upper bound: `<`, `<=`, or `=`, `~`, `^`, `*`
whose base version is below the running one; `>` and `>=` mark `Below`.
The target is, in order: the cached latest release when it satisfies the
requirement; the version of an inclusive upper bound written in full
(`<=0.6.2`, `=0.6.2`); the lowest version admitted by a lower bound
(`>=0.5`, `^0.5`, `~0.5.1`, missing parts as 0), checked against the whole
requirement; otherwise none. `core::doctor::evaluate` then writes
`codev self-update --version <target>`, or, without a target,
`codev self-update --version <X.Y.Z> with a release that satisfies "<req>"`.
`VersionFacts` gains `latest_known`, the cached latest release whether or
not it is newer, read offline as today.

**Alternatives considered**: always the lowest admitted version — rejected:
the cache, when it satisfies the requirement, is a release that exists and
is the most recent acceptable one. Fetching the release list — rejected:
doctor is offline by spec. Changing `codev self-update` to accept a
requirement (`--version "<0.7"`) — rejected here: a new interface for a
case the existing `--version` covers.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [A top-level typo no longer stops the command] → it is reported on every
  run of `codev status`, by `codev doctor`, and fails
  `codev validate --strict`, which CI runs.
- [The known-key lists drift from the structs] → the "every known key"
  test fails as soon as a field is added without its name.
- [The lowest admitted version may not be a published release] → it is the
  third choice, after the cache and an exact bound; `codev self-update
  --version` fails cleanly with `update_download_failed` if it does not
  exist, and the docs say to pick a release from the releases page.
- [Line numbers come from a text scan, not the YAML parser] → only used to
  point at the key; a miss falls back to line 1, never to a wrong file.
- [A new doctor check changes the count of every doctor report] → ids are
  additive in the v1 contract; docs samples are updated.

## Migration Plan

None for projects. Teams that add a key known only to this release or a
later one should set `codev_version` accordingly: codev 0.5 and earlier
still reject the file, and the documentation says so.

# Proposal: Forward-compatible configuration

## Why

`_codev/config.yaml` is rejected as a whole as soon as it holds a key the
running codev does not know, so a teammate whose codev is older than the
project's configuration gets a hard failure on every command — at the very
moment codev should explain that a newer version is required (`codev_version`
is the first such key).

## What Changes

- An unknown top-level key of `_codev/config.yaml` no longer fails the
  command: it is ignored, the rest of the configuration is used, and a
  warning `unknown_config_key` names the key, says the project may need a
  newer codev — quoting the project's `codev_version` when set — and points
  to `codev self-update`.
- Unknown keys inside the `mcp` section are tolerated the same way. Unknown
  keys inside an `inherits` entry or the `changelog` section still fail the
  command, because ignoring them would silently change which source is read
  or what `codev changelog --write` writes; that error now also quotes the
  project's `codev_version` when set.
- Unknown keys of an inherited source's configuration are ignored without a
  warning: only its context and rules are read.
- The warning appears in `codev status` (and every command that already
  reports configuration warnings), and as a `warning` finding of a new
  `config` item in `codev validate` (so `codev validate --strict` fails on
  it).
- Out of scope: a dedicated `codev doctor` check for unknown keys and the
  `codev self-update --version` fix of doctor's `codev_version` check are
  handled by a separate change.
- Documentation: configuration reference (unknown keys, forward
  compatibility, codev 0.5 and earlier still reject unknown keys), FAQ entry
  for a teammate whose codev fails on the configuration, the validate
  `config` item kind, in English and French.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `configuration` — how `_codev/config.yaml` treats keys the running codev
  does not know, and where that is reported.

### Modified Capabilities

None.

### Removed Capabilities

None.

## Impact

- `codev-core`: the unknown-key message.
- `codev-engine`: configuration loading (tolerant top level and `mcp`,
  strict `inherits` entries and `changelog`, error enriched with
  `codev_version`), the configuration warning, the `config` item of the
  validation report.
- `codev-cli`: the `config` item kind in the human and JSON validation
  reports (additive value of `kind`).
- Documentation in English and French: reference/configuration.md,
  reference/json-output.md (validate item kinds), faq.md.

## Release note

- Changed: A key of `_codev/config.yaml` that your codev does not know —
  typically one added by a newer codev — is now a warning `unknown_config_key`
  instead of an error, naming the key and the project's `codev_version`, and
  pointing to `codev self-update`; `codev validate --strict` reports it.
  codev 0.5 and earlier still reject such keys.

## Purpose

Describes how codev reads `_codev/config.yaml` when it holds keys the
running codev does not know — typically keys added by a newer codev — so
that an older binary keeps working and explains what it needs, while typos
stay visible.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Unknown top-level and `mcp` keys warn instead of failing

When `_codev/config.yaml` holds a top-level key, or a key of the `mcp`
section, that the running codev does not know, every command that reads
the configuration SHALL ignore that key, use the rest of the configuration,
and report one warning with the code `unknown_config_key` per unknown key.
The warning MUST name the key (`mcp.<key>` for a key of `mcp`), say that the
project may need a newer codev, quote the project's `codev_version`
requirement when the file sets one, and point to `codev self-update`.
Commands that report configuration warnings, `codev status` among them,
MUST report it in their human output and in the `status` array of their
JSON output. The keys of an inherited source's configuration MUST NOT
produce this warning: only its context and rules are read.

#### Scenario: Unknown top-level key with a version requirement

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` holds
  `codev_version: ">=0.9"` and the top-level key `review_policy`, unknown
  to the running codev, with an active change
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status --json`
- **THEN** the command succeeds and reports the change's status
- **AND** its `status` array holds a warning with the code
  `unknown_config_key` whose message names `review_policy`, quotes
  `>=0.9` and names `codev self-update`

#### Scenario: Unknown top-level key without a version requirement

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` holds `shema: spec-driven`
  and no `codev_version`, with an active change
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status`
- **THEN** the command succeeds with the default schema
- **AND** a warning `unknown_config_key` names `shema` and says the project
  may need a newer codev

#### Scenario: Unknown key of the `mcp` section

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` holds
  `mcp: {jira_tool: mcp__a__getJiraIssue, design_tool: mcp__b__get}`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update`
- **THEN** the skills are installed with the Jira tool `mcp__a__getJiraIssue`
- **AND** a warning `unknown_config_key` names `mcp.design_tool`

#### Scenario: Unknown key of an inherited source

- **GIVEN** a project inheriting from a local source whose
  `_codev/config.yaml` holds the unknown key `review_policy` and a context
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status`
- **THEN** the source's context is used
- **AND** no `unknown_config_key` warning is reported

### Requirement: Unknown keys of `inherits` entries and `changelog` fail the command

An unknown key inside an `inherits` entry or inside the `changelog` section
of `_codev/config.yaml` MUST make every command that reads the
configuration fail with the code `invalid`, naming the key, because
ignoring it would silently change which source is read or what
`codev changelog --write` writes. When the file sets `codev_version`, the
error message MUST also quote the requirement and point to
`codev self-update`.

#### Scenario: Unknown key of the `changelog` section

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` holds
  `codev_version: ">=0.9"` and `changelog: {since: v1.0.0}`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status`
- **THEN** the command fails with the code `invalid`
- **AND** the message names `since`, quotes `>=0.9` and names
  `codev self-update`

#### Scenario: Unknown key of an `inherits` entry

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` declares
  `inherits: [{path: ~/shared, pin: abc}]` and no `codev_version`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status`
- **THEN** the command fails with the code `invalid` naming `pin`

### Requirement: `codev validate` reports unknown configuration keys

When it validates the whole project — no scope, or `--all` — and
`_codev/config.yaml` holds unknown top-level or `mcp` keys, `codev validate`
SHALL add to its report an item of kind `config`, named `config`, whose path
is `_codev/config.yaml`, carrying one finding of severity `warning` and
code `unknown_config_key` per unknown key, at the line of that key. The
item MUST be absent when the configuration holds no unknown key, and from
the reports of `--changes`, `--specs` and of a named item. Like any warning,
it fails `codev validate --strict` and not `codev validate`.

#### Scenario: Strict validation with an unknown key

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` holds the unknown
  top-level key `review_policy` on line 3, and no other finding
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate --strict --json`
- **THEN** the report holds an item of kind `config` with one `warning`
  finding `unknown_config_key` at line 3 of `_codev/config.yaml`
- **AND** the exit code is 1

#### Scenario: Non-strict validation with an unknown key

- **GIVEN** the same project
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate`
- **THEN** the warning is reported and the exit code is 0

#### Scenario: Clean configuration

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` holds only known keys
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate --all --json`
- **THEN** no item of kind `config` is reported

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: `codev doctor` runs a fixed list of read-only checks

`codev doctor` SHALL evaluate the following checks, reported in this order, each
with a stable `id`, and report each one as `ok`, `missing` or `warning`,
with a stable `code` (`ok` when the check passes), a one-line message and,
when not `ok`, a one-line fix naming the exact command or skill:

| id | passes when | otherwise | code | fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `config.rules` | `rules:` has at least one entry, inherited ones included | missing | `rules_missing` | `/codev-configure` |
| `config.language` | `language:` is set in `_codev/config.yaml` | missing | `language_missing` | add `language: <code>` to `_codev/config.yaml` |
| `config.keys` | `_codev/config.yaml` holds no key the running codev ignores (top level or `mcp`) | warning | `unknown_config_key` | `codev self-update` when the running codev does not satisfy `codev_version`, otherwise correct or remove the key, naming the keys |
| `skills` | every configured workflow has its skill, generated by the running codev version | missing | `skills_missing` or `skills_outdated` | `codev update` |
| `sources` | every inherited git source is pinned in `_codev/codev.lock` and present in the cache, and the lock pins no undeclared source | missing (unpinned or not cached) or warning (undeclared pin) | `source_unpinned` or `lock_stale` | `codev sources update` |
| `codev_version` | the running codev satisfies the project's `codev_version`, when set, and the cached update check knows no newer release | missing (requirement not satisfied) or warning (newer release known) | `codev_version_unsatisfied` or `update_available` | `codev self-update`, or `codev self-update --version <X.Y.Z>` when the running codev is above the requirement |
| `specs` | at least one main spec exists | missing | `no_main_spec` | `/codev-propose`, noting that documenting existing behavior is planned work |
| `decisions` | at least one decision is `accepted`, local or inherited | warning | `no_accepted_decision` | `codev decision new "<title>"` |
| `validate` | `codev validate` reports no error and no warning | missing (errors) or warning (warnings only) | `validate_errors` or `validate_warnings` | `codev validate` |
| `claude_md` | `CLAUDE.md` holds the codev managed section | missing | `claude_md_section_missing` | `codev init` |
| `ci` | a file of `.github/workflows/` or `.gitlab-ci.yml` runs `codev validate` | missing | `ci_validate_missing` | `codev init` on GitHub, otherwise add `codev validate --strict` to the pipeline |
| `pr_template` | the pull request template holds the codev managed section — GitHub repositories only | missing | `pr_template_section_missing` | `codev init` |
| `changelog` | `CHANGELOG.md` exists and its managed `[Unreleased]` section matches what `codev changelog` would generate now | warning | `changelog_missing` (no file) or `changelog_outdated` | `codev changelog --write` |

The `pr_template` check MUST be absent from the report when the repository
is not a GitHub repository. A project without any inherited source passes
`sources`. A CI line is recognized when it names `codev` and then
`validate`, so `cargo run --bin codev -- validate` counts.

When the running codev does not satisfy `codev_version` because it is
above the requirement's upper bound, the fix MUST be
`codev self-update --version <X.Y.Z>`, a plain `codev self-update` refusing
to downgrade. `X.Y.Z` is, in this order of preference: the latest release
known to the update cache, when it satisfies the requirement; the highest
version the requirement admits, when an upper bound names it exactly (`<=`
or `=` with a full version); the lowest version the requirement admits,
when it has a lower bound. When none applies, the fix names the
requirement and asks for a release that satisfies it. When the running
codev is below the requirement, the fix stays `codev self-update`.

The `codev_version` check reads the per-user update cache that
`codev status` maintains and never refreshes it: with no cache, or with
`CI` set or `CODEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`, it only evaluates the requirement.

`codev doctor` MUST NOT write any file or access the network. The only
process it MAY spawn is `git`, for the local, read-only queries the
`changelog` check needs; outside a git repository, that check compares
with every archived change. Outside a codev project, it fails with the code
`no_codev_root`.

#### Scenario: A freshly initialized project

- **GIVEN** a project just initialized with `codev init --yes` outside
  GitHub, without rules, specs or decisions, and no newer codev release
  known
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `config.rules` and `specs` are `missing`, `decisions` is a
  `warning`, `ci` is `missing`
- **AND** `config.keys`, `config.language`, `skills`, `sources`,
  `codev_version`, `claude_md` and `validate` are `ok`
- **AND** `changelog` is a `warning` with the code `changelog_missing`
- **AND** no `pr_template` check is reported

#### Scenario: Outdated skills

- **GIVEN** a project whose skills were generated by an earlier codev
  version
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `skills` is `missing` with the code `skills_outdated` and the fix
  `codev update`

#### Scenario: An unpinned git source

- **GIVEN** a project declaring a git source absent from
  `_codev/codev.lock`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `sources` is `missing` with the code `source_unpinned` and the
  fix `codev sources update`

#### Scenario: CI recognized through `cargo run`

- **GIVEN** a GitHub project whose `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs
  `cargo run --bin codev -- validate --strict`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `ci` is `ok`

#### Scenario: Doctor writes nothing

- **GIVEN** any codev project
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** no file of the project is created or modified

#### Scenario: Outside a codev project

- **GIVEN** a folder with no `_codev/` above it
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** the command fails with the code `no_codev_root`

#### Scenario: CHANGELOG.md up to date

- **GIVEN** a project where `codev changelog --write` was just run
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `changelog` is `ok`

#### Scenario: CHANGELOG.md behind the archive

- **GIVEN** a project whose `CHANGELOG.md` managed section predates the
  latest archived change
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `changelog` is a `warning` with the code `changelog_outdated`
  and the fix `codev changelog --write`
- **AND** the exit code of `codev doctor --strict` is unaffected by it

#### Scenario: Running codev below the project's requirement

- **GIVEN** a project with `codev_version: ">=0.7"` and codev 0.6.0 running
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `codev_version` is `missing` with the code
  `codev_version_unsatisfied` and the fix `codev self-update`

#### Scenario: A newer release is known

- **GIVEN** a project without `codev_version`, and an update cache knowing
  a release newer than the running codev
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `codev_version` is a `warning` with the code `update_available`
  and the fix `codev self-update`
- **AND** no network request is made

#### Scenario: Running codev above the project's requirement

- **GIVEN** a project with `codev_version: ">=0.5, <0.7"`, codev 0.7.1
  running, and an update cache whose latest known release is 0.6.4
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `codev_version` is `missing` with the code
  `codev_version_unsatisfied` and the fix
  `codev self-update --version 0.6.4`

#### Scenario: Running codev above an exact upper bound, no usable cache

- **GIVEN** a project with `codev_version: "<=0.6.2"`, codev 0.7.0 running,
  and no update cache
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `codev_version` is `missing` with the fix
  `codev self-update --version 0.6.2`

#### Scenario: Running codev above a requirement with no exact bound

- **GIVEN** a project with `codev_version: "^0.5"`, codev 0.6.0 running, and
  an update cache whose latest known release, 0.6.0, does not satisfy it
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `codev_version` is `missing` with the fix
  `codev self-update --version 0.5.0`

#### Scenario: An unknown configuration key

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` holds the top-level key
  `review_policy`, unknown to the running codev, which satisfies
  `codev_version`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `config.keys` is a `warning` with the code `unknown_config_key`
  whose message names `review_policy`
- **AND** its fix tells to correct or remove the key
- **AND** the exit code of `codev doctor --strict` is unaffected by it

#### Scenario: An unknown key with an unsatisfied requirement

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` holds an unknown key and
  `codev_version: ">=9"`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev doctor`
- **THEN** `config.keys` is a `warning` with the fix `codev self-update`

# Tasks

Every task's definition of done also includes `cargo fmt --all --check`,
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test --workspace --locked`, all passing. Tests follow the project's
conventions: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code,
behavior-describing names, the in-memory `MemoryFileSystem` and `FixedEnv`
ports (through the CLI `Harness`) in engine and CLI tests, never a
temporary directory, no assumption about path separators or line endings.

## 1. Core: downgrade target and doctor checks

- [x] 1.1 In `codev_core::update`, add `RequirementSide` and
  `requirement_side(requirement, current)` (`Above` for a failing upper
  bound, `Below` otherwise, `None` when satisfied or unparsable), and
  `downgrade_target(requirement, latest_known)` (cached latest when it
  satisfies, else the full inclusive upper bound, else the lowest admitted
  version of a lower bound, else `None`), verified by unit tests
  `a_version_above_an_upper_bound_is_above`,
  `a_version_below_a_lower_bound_is_below`,
  `the_downgrade_target_prefers_the_cached_release`,
  `the_downgrade_target_falls_back_to_an_exact_upper_bound`,
  `the_downgrade_target_falls_back_to_the_lowest_admitted_version`,
  `no_downgrade_target_without_any_bound`.
- [x] 1.2 In `codev_core::doctor`, add `latest_known` to `VersionFacts` and
  give the `codev_version` check the fix `codev self-update --version
  <target>` (or the placeholder naming the requirement) when the running
  codev is above, `codev self-update` when below, verified by unit tests
  `codev_version_above_the_bound_fixes_with_an_explicit_version`
  (doctor: "Running codev above the project's requirement", "Running codev
  above an exact upper bound, no usable cache", "Running codev above a
  requirement with no exact bound"),
  `codev_version_above_without_any_target_names_the_requirement` and the

- [x] 1.3 Add the `config.keys` check after `config.language` (fact

  satisfied, otherwise "correct or remove"; update `CHECK_IDS` and the

  `unknown_config_keys_with_an_unsatisfied_requirement_fix_with_self_update`,

messages: I've rewritten the proposal. Now running `codev validate`.

I removed the `doctor` capability from the proposal, so it now covers only the configuration that tolerates unknown keys. I only edited `_codev/changes/forward-compatible-config/proposal.md`.

**What changed in the proposal:**
- **Why:** removed the paragraph about `codev doctor` suggesting a `codev self-update` that refuses to downgrade.
- **What Changes:** removed the `config.keys` check and the `codev self-update --version <X.Y.Z>` fix. Added a line saying both are out of scope and go to a separate change. The documentation item no longer mentions the doctor tables or samples.
- **Modified Capabilities:** now `None`. It used to list `doctor`.
- **Impact:** removed the doctor parts of each crate (the version upper-bound analysis, the downgrade target, the `config.keys` check, the doctor facts). Removed the doc pages touched only for doctor (`reference/cli.md`, `guides/repository-integration.md`, `quickstart.md`).
- **Release note:** no longer mentions `config.keys`, and the "Fixed" entry about `codev self-update --version` is gone.

**Ripple (reported, not applied):**
- **Orphaned spec:** `_codev/changes/forward-compatible-config/specs/doctor/spec.md` no longer matches any capability in the proposal. Suggested: delete it, or move it into the separate doctor change.
- **`design.md`:** two decisions are now outside the proposal: "A `config.keys` doctor check, a warning" and "The downgrade target is computed in the core". Doctor is also mentioned in the Context, the Goals ("doctor's version fix is a command that works"), the Non-goals and the Risks. Suggested: `/codev-update design` to remove them.
- **`tasks.md`:** tasks 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 are doctor-only. Task 3.1 includes the doctor facts and tests (`doctor_reports_an_unknown_config_key`, `doctor_fixes_a_codev_above_the_requirement_with_an_explicit_version`). Task 4.2 includes the doctor tables, the doctor samples and `grep config.keys`. Task 5.1 includes the `codev doctor` run. Suggested: `/codev-update tasks`.
- **Code already written:** every task in `tasks.md` is checked, so the doctor code is presumably already implemented. Those code changes would have to be reverted from this change or moved to the separate one. That is `/codev-apply`'s job once the specs and tasks are revised.

**`codev validate forward-compatible-config`:** 0 errors and 1 warning: `domains_missing` at `proposal.md:1`, because the proposal has no `## Domains` section. The original proposal had none either, so this was already there before my edit.

**Next step:** delete `specs/doctor/spec.md`, then run `/codev-update design` and `/codev-update tasks`, then `/codev-apply` to bring the code back in line.
